newsitem.title: USA: Clinton speaks at boisterous rally before debate.
newsitem.headline: Clinton speaks at boisterous rally before debate.

text.p: President Clinton addressed a boisterous rally outside his hotel before secluding himself for a final few hours of rest and rehearsal ahead of his debate Sunday night against Republican Bob Dole.

"Tonight I am going to have a chance to tell the American people what you know: We are better off than we were four years ago," Clinton told the rally of about 1,000 supporters, anticipating a likely line of attack in the debate.

Smiling and saluting the crowd, Clinton appeared buoyed by the 20-minute rally, which took place outside the Hastings Hotel in Hartford, where the 90-minute debate was scheduled to begin at 9 p.m. EDT.

After making a five-minute speech and shaking hands with supporters, often reaching deep into the crowd, Clinton jumped onto the stage to acknowledge the loud applause and shouts of "Four more years!"
He then smiled, clapped his hands and disappeared into the hotel.
Clinton was expected to spend his last hours before the debate resting, although White House spokesman Mike McCurry said he was likely to take some time to go over his opening and closing statements.
Another top aide said there was likely to be one final "pepper session" during the afternoon, apparently a question- and-answer period to keep the president on his toes.

Clinton flew to Hartford from Chautauqua, New York, where he had been training for the debates for the past three days, and immediately took a tour of the debate hall, the Bushnell Theatre, to learn its layout.
McCurry told reporters he had asked the president during the flight how he felt about the debate, the first of two scheduled with Dole, and Clinton had replied, "I feel fine."
Another aide said the president was generally relaxed but added: "He's a little edgy. You've got to be."
